evidencia:
Page: Kellock–Taschereau Commission. Sentence: The Kellock–Taschereau Commission (officially the Royal Commission to Investigate the Facts Relating to and the Circumstances Surrounding the Communication, by Public Officials and Other Persons in Positions of Trust of Secret and Confidential Information to Agents of a Foreign Power) was a royal commission appointed by Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King on behalf of the Government of Canada under Order in Council PC 411 on February 5, 1946.
Page: William Lyon Mackenzie King. Sentence: A Liberal with 21 years and 154 days in office, he was the longest-serving prime minister in Canadian history.

Facts:
- On February 5, 1946, the Government of Canada appointed the Kellock–Taschereau Commission under Order in Council PC 411.
- The Kellock–Taschereau Commission was officially named the Royal Commission to Investigate the Facts Relating to and the Circumstances Surrounding the Communication, by Public Officials and Other Persons in Positions of Trust of Secret and Confidential Information to Agents of a Foreign Power.
- Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King appointed the Kellock–Taschereau Commission on behalf of the Government of Canada.
- William Lyon Mackenzie King was a Liberal.
- William Lyon Mackenzie King served 21 years and 154 days in office, making him the longest-serving prime minister in Canadian history.
